canopy.note: Currently unused. Retained for pressed states on green surfaces.

display.purpose: The Splyt wordmark on the auth screens. Nothing else.

amount.purpose: Currency values that answer the screen's question. Scales to 36pt on hero cards.

page-title.purpose: The screen name, placed inside the body container, never in the header.

section-title.purpose: Group headings within a screen; also the stat-card value at 24pt/700.

card-title.purpose: The title of a single card; modal titles use it at 22pt/700.

body-strong.purpose: Inline values inside rows: member names, row amounts, menu labels.

label.purpose: Form field and stat labels in Faded Ink. Uppercase only on the hero eyebrow.

caption.purpose: Timestamps, helper text, pill text at 600, tab labels at 11pt.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: Every white card, stat card, event card, and menu surface. Android elevation 3. Deliberately near-subliminal.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: The toast only. Android elevation 6. The one element genuinely above the page.

shadows.name: edge
shadows.purpose: The tab bar's upward shadow, paired with a hairline top border. Android elevation 8.

shadows.name: control
shadows.purpose: The white circular back button on the green header, where tone alone cannot separate it. Android elevation 2.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: The modal backdrop tint behind bottom sheets.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.value: spring to scale(0.97) on pressIn, spring to 1 on pressOut (speed 40, bounciness 6)
motion.purpose: The tactile press response on AppButton. Paired with opacity 0.82.

motion.name: press-opacity
motion.purpose: Press feedback on rows, tiles, and icon buttons.

breakpoints.name: two-up

narrative.overview:
Splyt is what the group gathers around when the trip is over and the receipts come out. The system is built to feel like a table, not a bank: a deep forest-green header holds the top of every screen like a placemat, and a large pale panel slides up over it with rounded shoulders, carrying white cards that sit on the surface with almost no shadow. Nothing is dense, nothing is stacked tightly, and nothing shouts. The money is the loudest thing on any screen, and everything else stands back so it can be read at a glance, one-handed, in a hotel lobby at midnight.

The register is calm, unhurried, trustworthy, and precise. Precision here means legibility, not density: the system spends whitespace freely (8pt grid, 16pt screen margins, 12-16pt between cards) because a group arguing about who paid for dinner does not need a spreadsheet, it needs one clear number. Green is the identity, but it is rationed - the header, primary actions, focus rings, and selected states own it, and everything else is ink on paper. Components are tactile and confident: a press should feel like it landed, surfaces should feel like objects with weight, and state changes should be felt, not just seen.

The confirmed anti-reference is Splitwise's dense list UI. Splyt never turns into rows of hairline-separated text at the same size and weight. Each meaningful thing gets a card, a tap target, and room to breathe. The second thing it must never become is amateur - the palette is disciplined, the type scale is fixed, and the polish must read as professional and clean rather than decorated.
keyCharacteristics: Three-zone architecture on every authenticated screen: green header -> lifted body container -> white cards
Deep forest green (#2F6F57) as the only brand voice; everything else is ink, paper, and one signal green
System fonts on both platforms - no custom typeface, no brand font to load
Tonal layering over shadows; depth comes from white-on-gray, not from lift
Money is always the largest, heaviest element in its section
Icons are a single family (Material Community Icons), always outline variants
Page titles live inside the body container, never in the header

rules.name: The Rationed Green Rule
rules.body: Settled Forest appears in exactly three places on a screen: the header, the primary action, and the current selection. If a fourth green element appears, one of them is not actually primary.

rules.name: The Two Greens Are Not Interchangeable Rule
rules.body: Settled Forest means Splyt. Signal Green means live right now. Swapping them makes brand chrome look like a status and status look like decoration.

rules.name: The Ink Over Black Rule
rules.body: Text and dark fills use Receipt Ink (#1C1C1E), never #000. Pure black next to a soft green field reads as a rendering bug.

rules.name: The Bright Is A Fill Rule
rules.body: Signal Green, Info Blue, Danger Clay, and Warning Amber are fills only. A colored fill carries Receipt Ink on top; text in a semantic color uses that color's darkened text variant. White on #22C55E measures 2.28:1 and is banned.

rules.name: The Money Is The Headline Rule
rules.body: Within any card or section, the currency value is the largest and heaviest element present. If a label or title outweighs the number, the hierarchy is inverted.

rules.name: The Two Steps Rule
rules.body: A value sits one size step and one weight step above its own label - never one or the other. 13pt/500 Faded Ink label over 15pt/600 or larger Receipt Ink value.

rules.name: The No Shouting Rule
rules.body: No uppercase anywhere except the hero eyebrow label. Currency codes, statuses, and pills stay sentence case. Bold is for titles and money only, never for emphasis inside a sentence.

rules.name: The Flat Header Rule
rules.body: The header is a single flat Settled Forest fill. A gradient was tried and reverted: react-native-linear-gradient mis-measures the header on this RN version and clips the header row under the status bar. There are no gradients in this system.

rules.name: The Lifted Panel Rule
rules.body: The body container always overlaps the header by 20pt with 24pt top corners and square bottom corners. It never gains a shadow, a border, or bottom rounding.

rules.name: The One Content Margin Rule
rules.body: Every piece of content on a screen starts at the same 16pt margin, whatever container it sits in. A tinted section earns its emphasis by bleeding to the screen edges, never by insetting its text further than the text above and below it.

rules.name: The Title Lives Below Rule
rules.body: The page title belongs inside the body container, not in the green header. The header carries identity and navigation; the body carries content.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Content is a single scrolling column. Two-up is allowed only for stat cards and action tiles, and never three-up.

rules.name: The Green Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows use #163628, never black. A neutral shadow under a green-tinted UI reads as dirt.

rules.name: The Tone Before Lift Rule
rules.body: To separate two surfaces, change their tone first (white on Paper Gray, Morning Wash on white). Reach for a shadow only when tone cannot do it - which in practice means only the back button and the toast.

rules.name: The Radius Scales With Size Rule
rules.body: Bigger surface, rounder corner. Icon badge 8pt -> button 14pt -> card 16pt -> hero 20pt -> screen panel 24pt. Never give a small chip a 24pt radius or a full panel an 8pt one.

rules.name: The Outline Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons are outline-weight by default. A filled icon in a row of outlined ones reads as a selected state, so never introduce one casually.

dos: Do build every authenticated screen with AppScreen, preserving the green header -> -20pt lifted Paper Gray body -> white cards sequence.
Do put the page title inside the body container at Page Title size (28pt/700), with any subtitle in Body/Faded Ink directly beneath it.
Do make the currency value the largest and heaviest element in its card, one size and one weight step above its label.
Do route every currency value through MoneyValue, and state the sign in words with balanceLabel() so meaning survives without color.
Do hold to the 8pt grid - 16pt screen margins, 16pt card padding and gaps, 24pt for hero padding and between major sections.
Do use Settled Forest (#2F6F57) as the flat header fill, the single primary action, and the current selection - and stop there.
Do reserve Signal Green (#22C55E) for live status, and Info Blue (#3B82F6) for neutral/pending status.
Do give every field a visible Label above it, and signal focus with the 1.5pt Settled Forest border.
Do separate surfaces by tone (white on Paper Gray) before reaching for a shadow.
Do use outline-variant Material Community Icons via AppIcon, at 16 / 18 / 20pt.
Do keep every tap target at or above 44pt.
Do choose the black button for operational actions and the green button for brand-affirmative ones.
donts: Don't build dense hairline-separated list rows. Splitwise's list UI is the named anti-reference; give each item a card, a target, and space.
Don't put the page title in the green header, add a shadow to the body container, or round its bottom corners.
Don't use pure black (#000) for text, fills, or shadows - Receipt Ink (#1C1C1E) and shadow green (#163628) are the only darks.
Don't introduce a new accent hue. The palette is one green, two washes, one signal green, one blue, one clay.
Don't outline a card. Cards separate by tone and a 6% ambient shadow; borders belong to secondary buttons, focused/errored inputs, and selection marks only.
Don't raise shadow opacity to make a card pop. If it needs emphasis, change its tone (Sage Wash) or its size, not its lift.
Don't use uppercase anywhere except the hero card's eyebrow label, and don't bold text for emphasis mid-sentence.
Don't load a custom font. Both platforms use their system face deliberately.
Don't put green in the tab bar or add an active-tab indicator; ink weight carries the state.
Don't put white text on Signal Green, Success Green, Warning Amber, or Danger Clay - all four measure below 4.5:1. Use Receipt Ink on the fill, or the darkened text variant on a light surface.
Don't ship a gradient anywhere in the app, including the header. The system is flat fills and tonal layering.

Don't inset a tinted section's content past the 16pt screen margin. If a section needs emphasis at the top of a screen, bleed it to the edges with AppHeroBand rather than nesting a padded card inside a padded container.
Don't stack more than two items side by side.
